decide.sql: SELECT thinkthen_decide('Is this a complaint?', 'I demand a refund today');

probability.sql: SELECT thinkthen_probability('Is this a complaint?', 'I demand a refund today');

choose.sql: SELECT thinkthen_choose('Which team handles this?', 'refund now', ['the refund desk', 'other desk']);

score.sql: SELECT thinkthen_score('How strong is the refund claim?', 'maybe later', ['low', 'mid', 'high']);

tag.sql: SELECT thinkthen_tag('What is in this text?', 'the refund and the shipping', ['refund', 'shipping']);

details.sql: SELECT array_length(thinkthen_details('Is this a complaint?', 'I demand a refund today').requests);

usage.sql: SELECT metric, value FROM thinkthen_usage() ORDER BY metric;

warm.sql: SELECT thinkthen_warm('Is this a complaint?', t) FROM (SELECT unnest(['refund now', 'refund again']) t);

recognize.sql: SELECT t.text, t.kind FROM (SELECT unnest(thinkthen_recognize('Maria Chen joined Northwind Freight in Chicago last spring.', ['person', 'organization', 'place'])) AS t) ORDER BY t.text;

relations.sql: SELECT (u.r).name, (u.r).source, (u.r).target FROM (SELECT 'Northwind Freight is based in Chicago and Denver.' AS body) t, unnest(thinkthen_relations(t.body, '@names.json')) AS u(r);

setup: CREATE TABLE alerts(id INTEGER, body VARCHAR);

INSERT INTO alerts VALUES (1, 'Checkout returns 500 at the payment step.'), (2, 'Card charges are failing for every customer.'), (3, 'The nightly export ran two hours late.'), (4, 'The payments database ran out of disk space.');
relate.sql: SELECT * FROM thinkthen_relate('SELECT id, body FROM alerts', ['caused_by']);
